note: The five commercial motions a partner can run with the Lyzr stack. A motion is not a revenue shape (that is patterns.json) and not a use case: it is the relationship between a Lyzr product and the partner's existing business. One recommendation per motion, because three cards on the same motion are three versions of one conversation however different the use cases sound.

motions.label: Upsell into existing AI projects
motions.what: Add a layer to work the partner already delivers. The client already has agents in production; this governs them without replacing what they run.
motions.needs: a partner already building or running AI in production

motions.label: New infrastructure and services offering
motions.what: Enter a category the partner does not sell today, on the back of infrastructure or environment work they already do.
motions.sells_to: clients whose requirements rule out what the partner can offer now
motions.needs: infrastructure, private cloud or regulated delivery experience

motions.label: Expand existing delivery engagements
motions.what: Take an engagement the partner already runs and widen its scope with a Lyzr product, rather than starting a new line of business.
motions.sells_to: the engagement they are already inside
motions.needs: live build, integration or automation engagements

motions.label: Build reusable or branded IP
motions.what: Turn repeated delivery into something the partner owns and licenses, instead of rebuilding it per client.
motions.sells_to: every client of a product they ship themselves
motions.needs: a product, an accelerator or repeated identical builds

motions.label: Take a Lyzr solution to your segment
motions.what: Deploy a packaged Lyzr solution into a customer segment the partner already serves, instead of building the equivalent from scratch.
motions.sells_to: a segment they already have relationships in
motions.needs: clients in the segment the solution was built for
